So in an organization like a company or a federal agency which oversees both construction and operation of facilities, facilities meaning, you know, any kind of building, infrastructure, whatever, you have two budgets. You have the capital budget and the operations budget.

The capital budget pays for construction and major renovations, so like a new housing tower or a big chiller and associated HVAC ducting or something like that. And the operations budget, in turn, pays for day-to-day maintenance, employee salaries, overhead, and so on and so forth.

The capital budget usually allows for big contract awards and ribbon cuttings and other stuff that the politicians like, while operations is boring day-to-day stuff like replacing light bulbs and paying the janitor. So here's the oldest trick in the book, which has been employed again and again to cripple federal programs. You fund the capital budget in full, but insist that operations have to be self-sufficient somehow.

This technique has been tried again and again to defund and cripple anything from public housing to transit to any social service you like. sometimes Title I slum clearance, referring to the specific provision of the act which provided the federal funding.
